evidence.section: 1. Introduction to the Client-Server Model and the Socket Interface
3.2 Detailed Specification of Core Socket System Calls

question_links.rationale: The source locates the API across the user/kernel boundary; the socket-call lesson separates ordinary endpoints from privileged raw sockets. Together they explain the boundary, but do not support the key claiming ordinary applications need device-driver privilege.
question_links.next_action: Read the primary lesson and any additional required lessons. Optional links are background; review flagged wording before scored practice.
question_links.review_note: The API can include user-space library code while system calls enter the kernel stack. This does not require ordinary applications to obtain driver privileges; no option cleanly states the boundary issue.

evidence.section: 3. `bind()` — Assigning a Local Protocol Address
2. `connect()` — Initiating an Active Open (Client)

question_links.rationale: Bind chooses the local IP/port; connect supplies the remote endpoint and can otherwise let the kernel choose the local endpoint. Both explanations are needed for the API-separation tradeoff.
question_links.next_action: Read the primary lesson and any additional required lessons. Optional links are background; review flagged wording before scored practice.

evidence.section: 3. `bind()` — Assigning a Local Protocol Address

question_links.rationale: Bind names a local IP and port and documents EADDRINUSE for conflicts. The answer needs an overlapping local endpoint, not merely equal numeric ports on different local addresses.
question_links.next_action: Read the primary lesson and any additional required lessons. Optional links are background; review flagged wording before scored practice.
question_links.review_note: Specify overlapping local IP/port bindings in the same networking context. Equal port numbers on different local IPs do not alone establish a conflict.
